01 / Method

Learn with richer signals.
Deploy a compact policy.

XS-VLA uses two stages of training: coarse spatial supervision initializes the backbone, then a regularized demonstration latent conditions flow learning. Neither the teacher nor the posterior encoder is required at inference.

STAGE 01 · CSD

Spatial supervision for initialization

Coarse-Grained Spatial Distillation converts teacher-predicted object coordinates into nine symbolic region labels. This auxiliary task shapes the compact backbone’s initialization before policy training.

STAGE 02 · LFM

Demonstration-conditioned flow learning

Latent Flow Matching encodes state and demonstrated actions into a posterior latent that conditions the velocity field. KL regularization draws the posterior toward a Gaussian prior, whose mean replaces the encoder at deployment.

See the spatial-supervision pipeline

The teacher receives unmarked images. The grid overlay illustrates quantization. Diagnostics do not establish reliable instruction-conditioned localization; the measured benefit of CSD is in downstream control.

At deploymentImages + instruction + robot state → action chunk. No teacher query, spatial-label prediction, demonstration input, or posterior encoder.

Beyond image exposure

CSD + LFM reaches 90.25%, compared with 88.75% for matched image-only pretraining + LFM.

Beyond the regression loss

With CSD and Huber fixed, adding the posterior-conditioning and KL branch raises success from 86.50% to 90.25%.

03 / Physical manipulation

From simulation
to the robot table.

On three Mobile ALOHA tasks, average strict success rises from 21.7% to 65.0%. Each model is evaluated for 20 trials per task.

Cup placing

Base 45% →90%
XS-VLA: 18 / 20 successful trials

Dual-arm block stacking

Base 0% →30%
XS-VLA: 6 / 20 completed stacks

Sequential coordination

Base 20% →75%
XS-VLA: 15 / 20 successful trials

Both models use 80k policy-training steps. XS-VLA starts from the same 14k CSD checkpoint used for LIBERO. Reported stacking success requires a stable completed stack; partial credit is reported separately in the paper.

The demonstration video also shows XS-VLA operating on OpenARM, PiPER, and XLeRobot. These platform-specific deployments provide qualitative evidence across robot platforms.

04 / Deployment

A small policy,
measured on real hardware.

The full checkpoint has 244.83M parameters. Removing 0.84M training-only parameters leaves a 243.99M-parameter deployed policy, including the action expert.

GPULatency / chunkQuery rate
A100 PCIe 40GB259.93 ms3.85 Hz
RTX 3090321.08 ms3.11 Hz

Peak inference VRAM: 0.51 GiB on both GPUs. Batch size 1; two 256 × 256 images; BF16; 10 flow steps; 8 warm-up runs and 50 measurements. Tokenization, simulation, and video writing are excluded.

LIBERO generates 50 actions per query and executes 10 before replanning. Query rate measures model inference; it is distinct from amortized action throughput and robot servo frequency.
